Longer sales cycles.
A clearer shared picture.

Qualification with context

Capture what the prospective customer needs, relevant timing and the information needed for a useful conversation.

A pipeline that fits your sales process

Agree stages and ownership so every opportunity has a place, a responsible person and a next action.

Proposals that do not disappear

Keep quotation and proposal activity linked to the customer. Document and e-signature capabilities depend on agreed access and configuration.

Visibility for the whole team

Use current records and activity to review stalled opportunities, coach follow-through and plan the next conversation.

See the work behind the growth.

Understand where opportunities stand, where follow-up slows and what needs attention. Give your team more time for customers and a clearer basis for planning.

Illustrative quotation follow-up. No autonomous deal-closing or guaranteed revenue is implied.

Different decisions need different support

A process tailored to your sale.

A supplier may work with several decision-makers and a purchase order. A homeowner may need a site visit and a renovation quote. An event enquiry may depend on dates, requirements and a proposal. Agree the stages and information that fit your business.

As your team grows, review ownership, handoffs and reporting. Additional custom work, integrations and expanded scope are agreed separately.

For the person following up

Keep the buyer’s open question, quotation, decision date and next action together. Update the record after each useful conversation.

For the manager coaching the team

Use current opportunity context to discuss qualification, stalled proposals and workload. Agree the next action with the person responsible.

For the owner planning ahead

Review expected revenue and timing alongside capacity and payment assumptions. A pipeline supports planning, not guaranteed results.
